newsitem.title: USA: Florida police computer targets deadbeat parents.
newsitem.headline: Florida police computer targets deadbeat parents.

text.p: Florida parents who fail to pay child support will find themselves ranked alongside criminals and murderers in police computer files under a new state law.

The Florida Department of Law Enforcement, backed by a state law that began Oct. 1, has entered on the state computer network more than 4,000 names of parents who have been issued arrest warrants for non-payment of child support. The names can be checked by policemen making routine traffic stops.

Larry Fuchs, director of the state Department of Revenue, which collects child support payments, said the programme was an attempt to put a dent in the millions owed by estranged parents who turn their backs on their financial responsibilities to their children.

"This is a societal ill. This is not a government debt," Fuchs told reporters in Tallahassee. "This is what I consider to be the final piece of convincing deadbeat parents that there are real consequences if they don't pay. They are going to go to jail."
